One case per sentence. `label`: supported_claim (a statement about the business that the facts on file carry, in any wording), unsupported_claim (a statement about the business that nothing on file supports: the page may not say it until the owner confirms it), not_a_claim (generic statements, advice to the reader, the call to action, quotes from cited sources). `facts` per site: what Content QA reads as the business's own text (OWN_TEXT). `heading` / `h3` / `before` / `list`: where the sentence sits on the page (the check reads a sentence with its section); `section`: for the sentences of the exec 42 page, the whole H2 group they sit in on that page (the scorer reads that section in place of the heading fields). `holdout`: sha1(sentence + site) first byte mod 10 < 3, fixed here so a fixer reports dev and hold-out separately and tunes on dev only. Labels were written from the facts before the code was run and are not changed to pass. Scorer: score_claims.js; scenario CLACC ratchets on CLAIMS_BASELINE.md. Production group (2026-10-27, CL-Q01..CL-Q34, source "production pages 2026-10-27"): the 34 sentences of the four production page runs 949 / 2195 / 2552 / 2575 that Content QA flagged as unsupported statements about the client, labelled as R1_PIPELINE_ANALYSIS.md classifies them (`prod_class`: true_on_file, true_on_site, generic_advice, cta, invented). They are dev cases as a group (the fixer tuned on them); the hold-out is the older set.

## Build, buy or integrate: choosing the right AI approach

### Should we build, buy or integrate AI?

Start with the least custom option that meets the requirement. Buy AI already built into tools you license when the process is standard. Integrate and extend with Copilot Studio or AI Builder when you need your own data or workflows. Build on Azure OpenAI Service only when the use case is a differentiator or the data demands it.

**Build, buy or integrate: which AI route fits your use case**

| Route | Typical Microsoft tools | Best when | Integration depth | Data and compliance considerations | Skills your team needs afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy (out of the box) | Copilot for Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 Copilot | The process is standard, such as drafting or summarising | Low: works inside existing apps | Inherits current permissions, so fix oversharing and apply labels first | Admin configuration, user training |
| Integrate and extend | Copilot Studio, AI Builder, Power Platform | You need your own data, workflows or agents without full custom development | Medium: ERP and CRM connectors | Connector governance, data loss prevention policies | Makers and a platform owner |

- **Systems integrator or Microsoft partner:** Dynamics 365, data and security integration, plus support after go-live, such as Tech& Managed Services.

### Should we build, buy or integrate AI?

Start with the least custom option that meets the requirement. Buy AI already built into tools you license when the process is standard. Integrate and extend with Copilot Studio or AI Builder when you need your own data or workflows. Build on Azure OpenAI Service only when the use case is a differentiator or the data demands it.

| Route | Typical Microsoft tools | Best when | Integration depth | Data and compliance considerations | Skills your team needs afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy (out of the box) | Copilot for Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 Copilot | The process is standard, such as drafting or summarising | Low: works inside existing apps | Inherits current permissions, so fix oversharing and apply labels first | Admin configuration, user training |
| Integrate and extend | Copilot Studio, AI Builder, Power Platform | You need your own data, workflows or agents without full custom development | Medium: ERP and CRM connectors | Connector governance, data loss prevention policies | Makers and a platform owner |
| Build custom | Azure OpenAI Service, Azure AI Services | The use case is a differentiator or needs retrieval over proprietary documents | High: custom APIs and data pipelines | Region choice, network isolation, logging, model risk review | Developers, machine learning skills, MLOps |

## AI governance, data residency and UAE compliance

These are questions to put to any consultant, not legal advice. Confirm the obligations that apply to you with your legal and compliance teams.

Which data protection rules apply depends on where your entity is licensed and where personal information is processed.

### Questions to ask about data residency

- Where will personal data and backups be processed and stored?
- Which cloud region will host each component, and does any part run outside the UAE?
- Are prompts and outputs retained or used for training?
- Does federal law, DIFC or ADGM govern our entity?
- What audit evidence will show a regulator how a decision was made?

### Governance controls to have in place before going live

- Access permissions reviewed, because Copilot surfaces whatever a user can already open
- Sensitivity labels applied before switching on Copilot
- Human review for decisions affecting customers or citizens
- AI activity logged and retained in line with policy
- Model monitoring for accuracy and drift

### Can AI pass compliance review in banking and the public sector?

It can, when controls come first. Banks should ask what their regulator expects on model risk and audit trails. Public bodies should ask how government data classification applies. We design permissions, labels, logging and human review before any model touches live data, and document each decision for your audit team. a regional bank

We treat data as a sovereign asset. Read more about [our security approach](https://www.techand.ai/security).

## What does an AI consultant do?

The role bridges AI technologies and business management. A consultant decides where AI will change a decision or a cost, then gets it there safely. That needs in-depth knowledge of machine learning and generative AI. It also needs enough grasp of your operations to judge which AI models are worth funding. Work runs in phases, from discovery to governance. Each phase ends in a deliverable you review before you fund the next.

Fortune Business Insights projects a 26.60% CAGR for the global AI market, reaching $2,480.05 billion by 2034 ([source](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/artificial-intelligence-market-100114)). More providers mean more claims to vet, and the scorecard below helps you do that.

### Do AI consultants need industry domain expertise?

Yes. Use-case value, the meaning of the data and the applicable rules all differ by sector. A banking specialist asks about audit trails and model risk. A retail or manufacturing specialist focuses on demand and inventory data. Domain expertise shortens discovery and lowers delivery risk.

## What does an AI consultancy do for enterprises in Dubai?

An AI consultancy finds where artificial intelligence will create measurable value and checks whether your data is ready. It then designs, builds, governs and supports the solution. For Dubai enterprises that usually means AI strategy, machine learning and generative AI, intelligent automation, and compliance with UAE data protection rules.

Classic management consulting ends with a recommendation. An AI consulting company must own what comes next: the data, the build and adoption. That takes technical expertise, not just strategy.

### The service areas an AI consulting company covers

- AI strategy: use cases tied to business KPIs and a funding sequence.
- Data analytics and readiness: checking ERP, CRM and spreadsheet data can support a model.
- Machine learning and predictive analytics: forecasts, risk scores and anomaly flags.
- Natural language processing: reading and answering text in Arabic and English.
- Computer vision: inspecting images from production lines, documents or sites.
- Generative AI and copilots: drafting, summarising and searching your records.
- Intelligent automation and process automation: moving work between systems with fewer manual steps.
- AI governance: policies, controls and monitoring that pass internal audit.

Tech& is a Microsoft partner based in Dubai Airport Freezone (DAFZA). We serve enterprises across the United Arab Emirates and the GCC and bring 20+ years of industry experience. Demand is rising. Fortune Business Insights projects the global AI consulting services market will "grow from $11.91 billion in 2026 to $73.89 billion by 2034" ([source](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/ai-consulting-services-market-111179)).
